memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'We both had dreams,' they answered, 'but there is no one to interpret them.' Then Joseph said to them, 'Do not interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.'" - Gen 40:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The two men are troubled because they have had strange dreams and there is no one to explain them. In Egypt, dream-interpreting was the work of professional magicians and wise men — and none were available in prison. But Joseph responds with a question that quietly redirects everything: "Do not interpretations belong to God?"

Here is Joseph's humility and faith on display. He does not boast, "I have a special power to interpret dreams." He points away from himself and up to God. Whatever gift Joseph had, he knew its source. Any wisdom or ability he possessed came from the Lord, and he was careful to give God the credit.

This is a mark of a truly godly person: they deflect glory to God rather than gather it to themselves. When we are gifted, praised, or successful, the temptation is to take the credit and let people admire us. Joseph shows a better way — to say, in effect, "This is not about me; it belongs to God."

What gifts and abilities do you have? Whatever they are, they came from the Lord's hand (1 Cor 4:7; Jas 1:17). We are meant to use them well, but always to point the praise back to God. Let your talents be a window through which others see Him, not a mirror that only reflects you. Give God the glory for whatever He has given you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I point praise back to God, or gather it to myself?
2. Do I remember that my gifts come from the Lord?
3. How can my abilities be a window to God rather than a mirror of me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, everything I have comes from You. Keep me from taking the glory for Your gifts. Help me to use my abilities well and to point all the praise back to You, their true source. Amen.
